content.text: Would it make sense to split this work into two tickets:
Verify files on disk against their counterparts imported in a Fedora
Verify resources in a Fedora are the same as their exported counterparts on disk
- yes, I think that would make sense.   I can do that later today, if that sounds good.
, that would be great.
Hi
, Can I change this bug to one of the two and then create a new one for the other, or should this issue remain around with 2  related issues?
, yes, please, change this ticket and add another one.

, you can decide as this effort progresses whether the script/utility for verification is one or two. I can imagine that you simply produce one script/utility that looks at two things to see that they are the same: fedora repository, files on disk.
In that sense, it may not matter if you are verifying an export or an import.
Moving
's comment from
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2204
over here:
"[~bseeger, I started trying out a few ideas for verification scripts here:
https://github.com/jwestgard/fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests
This is not really the sort of general-purpose tool envisioned by the ticket, I think, but maybe it's food for thought."
I just created this repo:
https://github.com/bseeger/fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests
It's a work in progress, however it
will

l verify that all the items on disk are currently in fedora4.  I call that an export test, but I'm not so sure that it is actually.   The reverse test is not yet implemented and coming soon (once the code added to walk every resource in the fedora 4 system and see if it's on disk is written).  Ideally both tests would be run to verify that there are no missing / extra records sitting around.
Can someone other then me give it a spin, in what I call 'export' mode?
I tested it on the LUBM data set - once where they matched completely and once where I tweaked/deleted a few things in Fedora4.  It picked up the differences just fine.
And actually, this will probably die if you work with any binaries, since I haven't tested that yet (none in LUBM).
And once it does work with binaries, we can probably roll
's fixity check into it.
One initial comment: It would be great if this script were able to simply read the
importexport.config
created by the import/export utility... since the configuration information has significant overlap.
Hi
- sounds like a great idea, I'll look into that.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify
Current codebase ready for testing and review/approval, as of the import/export sprint 3 kickoff:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify
My first test was to:
manually create some simple resources in Fedora
export them
then run the verify.py
AttributeError: 'Config' object has no attribute 'bin'
This should not be a required configuration element.

Thanks, Andrew. I think the solution here is for us to know how to set the value of config.bin when there is no -b flag in the config (i.e. set it to the location of the exported binaries).  Once -binDir and -descDir are removed (
) what can we count on in terms of values that will always be present in the import-export config?
has been resolved. There should always be a path in the config now. Does that help?

, yes, that helps. So if I'm understanding correctly the resulting config file will now have a -d with a path to the location of both binaries and rdf resources. We'll need to rewrite the verifcation tool accordingly.
here is some sample output:
$ java -jar target/fcrepo-import-export-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar --mode export --resource http://localhost:8080/rest --dir /home/nruest/tmp/import-export-sprint-03/test/fcrepo-2226 --binaries

-m
export
-r
http://localhost:8080/rest
-d
/home/nruest/tmp/import-export-sprint-03/test/fcrepo-2226
-b
Thanks,
.  I've created a separate ticket for this issue: FCREPO-2332.
Resolved with resolving
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2332
The goal is to create a tool that will verify that data exported to disk, via the import-export client, is the same as what was in the original fedora system.

comments.body:
Would it make sense to split this work into two tickets:

  • Verify files on disk against their counterparts imported in a Fedora
  • Verify resources in a Fedora are the same as their exported counterparts on disk
Andrew Woods - yes, I think that would make sense. I can do that later today, if that sounds good.
Bethany Seeger, that would be great.
Hi Andrew Woods, Can I change this bug to one of the two and then create a new one for the other, or should this issue remain around with 2 related issues?
Bethany Seeger, yes, please, change this ticket and add another one.

Bethany Seeger, you can decide as this effort progresses whether the script/utility for verification is one or two. I can imagine that you simply produce one script/utility that looks at two things to see that they are the same: fedora repository, files on disk.
In that sense, it may not matter if you are verifying an export or an import.

Moving Joshua Allan Westgard's comment from https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2204 over here:

"[~bseeger, I started trying out a few ideas for verification scripts here: https://github.com/jwestgard/fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests

This is not really the sort of general-purpose tool envisioned by the ticket, I think, but maybe it's food for thought."

Andrew Woods, Joshua Allan Westgard,
I just created this repo: https://github.com/bseeger/fcrepo-sample-dataset-tests

It's a work in progress, however it will l verify that all the items on disk are currently in fedora4. I call that an export test, but I'm not so sure that it is actually. The reverse test is not yet implemented and coming soon (once the code added to walk every resource in the fedora 4 system and see if it's on disk is written). Ideally both tests would be run to verify that there are no missing / extra records sitting around.

Can someone other then me give it a spin, in what I call 'export' mode?

I tested it on the LUBM data set - once where they matched completely and once where I tweaked/deleted a few things in Fedora4. It picked up the differences just fine.

And actually, this will probably die if you work with any binaries, since I haven't tested that yet (none in LUBM).

And once it does work with binaries, we can probably roll Joshua Allan Westgard's fixity check into it.

One initial comment: It would be great if this script were able to simply read the importexport.config created by the import/export utility... since the configuration information has significant overlap.
Hi Andrew Woods- sounds like a great idea, I'll look into that.
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify

Current codebase ready for testing and review/approval, as of the import/export sprint 3 kickoff:

https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export-verify

My first test was to:

  • manually create some simple resources in Fedora
  • export them
  • then run the verify.py
AttributeError: 'Config' object has no attribute 'bin'

This should not be a required configuration element.

Thanks, Andrew. I think the solution here is for us to know how to set the value of config.bin when there is no -b flag in the config (i.e. set it to the location of the exported binaries). Once -binDir and -descDir are removed ( FCREPO-2226 Closed ) what can we count on in terms of values that will always be present in the import-export config?
Joshua Allan Westgard FCREPO-2226 Closed has been resolved. There should always be a path in the config now. Does that help?

Nick Ruest, yes, that helps. So if I'm understanding correctly the resulting config file will now have a -d with a path to the location of both binaries and rdf resources. We'll need to rewrite the verifcation tool accordingly.

Joshua Allan Westgard here is some sample output:

$ java -jar target/fcrepo-import-export-0.0.1-SNAPSHOT.jar --mode export --resource http://localhost:8080/rest --dir /home/nruest/tmp/import-export-sprint-03/test/fcrepo-2226 --binaries

-m
export
-r
http://localhost:8080/rest
-d
/home/nruest/tmp/import-export-sprint-03/test/fcrepo-2226
-b
Thanks, Nick Ruest. I've created a separate ticket for this issue: FCREPO-2332 Closed .
